About AskJamie™

AskJamie™ is the strategic intelligence layer that unifies your digital ecosystem. It orchestrates reasoning patterns, narrative logic, and architectural discipline across all derivative systems. By design, it blends clarity with creative range, enabling a cohesive experience from professional tooling to symbolic frameworks. The mission is straightforward: deliver consistent, high‑signal guidance that reflects a forward‑thinking, system‑driven approach to identity, design, and decision‑making.

AskJamie™ serves as the backbone for specialized modules — each purpose‑built, enterprise‑ready, and governed by a shared operating standard. It converts complexity into structure, prototypes ideas into frameworks, and maintains continuity across the broader AskJamie ecosystem.
Who Jamie is
Imagine the vintage tech guy at the back counter of a small‑town help desk — the one who actually listens to your whole question before reaching for a tool.
Calm under pressure
Jamie’s job is to lower the temperature in the room. Muted teals, paper grain, steady pacing — the visual identity is part of the answer, not a costume.
Diagram‑ready
When a sentence won’t do, Jamie reaches for a decision tree, a tradeoff table, or a Mermaid flow. The goal is always: leave you with something you can show someone else.
Architected, not improvised
Every persona in the Lens System (a set of focused ways to examine a story or challenge) has a written brief, a tone charter, and a guardrail set. Jamie isn’t winging it — Jamie has been built.
What AskJamie™ is not
Saying what something is not is part of saying what it is. Here’s where Jamie deliberately doesn’t play.
Not a chatbot platform
Jamie is an AI persona, not a vendor product, not a builder, and not a SaaS tool you license per seat. The lenses live as curated GPTs, not as an account you sign up for.
Not a general assistant
Jamie is scoped on purpose. Each lens has a job: portfolio storytelling, brand‑safety guardrails, enterprise discovery, résumé translation. Outside of those, Jamie politely points elsewhere.
Not impersonation

The BrandGuard™ (our AI brand-voice protection) GPTs work strictly from publicly available information about each brand. They are demonstrations of guardrail design, not impersonations of the brands themselves.
Who this is for
Job seekers & consultants
People who need their professional story translated into the language a hiring committee or a buyer will recognize, without losing what makes them specific.
Brand & marketing leads
Teams thinking about how a custom GPT should behave at the edges — tone, refusals, ethics, and the cases that aren’t in the brand book yet.
Enterprise practitioners
Anyone building in‑house AI investigator or research workflows who would rather start from a working recipe pack than a blank prompt.
What this site demonstrates
This repository is itself a portfolio artifact — a proof of what intentional, discipline-driven static-site development looks like in 2026.
Static-site discipline
Pure HTML/CSS/JS, zero build tools, zero frameworks. Every quality gate, script, and audit convention is explicit, reproducible, and documented in the repo.

· How AskJamie™ Works
From messy context to a useful next move.
AskJamie™ is an interpretive layer: a calm way to examine a story, challenge, or body of information before deciding how to express it.

The method does not promise an all-purpose answer. It gives the right question a focused lens, clear boundaries, and an output you can inspect, share, and act on. BrandGuard™ demonstrations use brand-voice protection patterns to make those boundaries visible.
The four-part journey
AskJamie starts with the material you already have. The work is not magic; it is disciplined framing.
1. Bring the mess
Share the draft, question, experience, research, or competing priorities. Context is useful even when it is incomplete.
2. Choose a lens
Select the focused way of seeing that fits the moment: career identity, portfolio proof, enterprise signals, or brand fidelity.
3. Interpret with guardrails
The lens separates evidence from assumption, names tradeoffs, and keeps its tone and scope visible instead of pretending every question is the same.
4. Leave with something usable
The output may be a clearer explanation, decision tree, brief, checklist, or next question — something ready for human review and the next conversation.
The Lens System keeps the voice consistent
A lens is a focused method for examining and expressing a story or challenge. The lenses share an interpretive standard, not hidden memory or a connected data pipeline.

That distinction matters. Résumé Representative does not silently inform Professional Portfolio. Enterprise Sleuth does not make a claim on behalf of a company. Each lens has a job, a boundary, and a public page that explains what it demonstrates.

· GPT‑AJ03: Enterprise Sleuth™
Your AI detective for enterprise knowledge.
Enterprise Sleuth turns modern AI into a curious, disciplined investigator that can search, connect, and explain what’s really going on across your documents, systems, and decisions.

Part detective, part analyst, part teacher — it’s a working example of how your own brand‑safe AI agents can make sense of messy SharePoint folders, sprawling knowledge bases, and years of “tribal knowledge”.

About Enterprise Sleuth
A reference “enterprise detective” and recipe pack for building your own brand‑aligned AI agents — across ChatGPT Custom GPTs, Copilot Studio agents, Gemini Gems, Claude projects, and similar tools.
Contextual Intelligence Retrieval
Enterprise Sleuth doesn’t just search for keywords. It pulls timelines, exceptions, and relationships from across your files so answers are grounded in your reality — not generic internet wisdom.

Turns your organization into a map, not a maze. It learns who is connected to what, where information lives, and how work really flows, so you can ask “who knows this?”, “what did we try last time?”, or “what’s blocking this?” and get a coherent story back.

Helps you trace decisions back to policies, approvals, and context. Perfect for audits, onboarding, and those “why did we do it this way?” conversations that usually send people spelunking through email threads.
From demo GPT to repeatable recipe

The GPT you open in ChatGPT is tuned to OverKill Hill P³™ (the R&D studio behind AskJamie)’s own knowledge as a live example. The actual “product” is a package of prompts, instruction patterns, knowledge‑file structures, and step‑by‑step guidance that you can port into your own stack — to build a brand ambassador, sales agent, research assistant, governance aide, or whatever force‑multiplier you need.

In other words: you’re not buying another chatbot. You’re licensing a battle‑tested way of thinking about agents that’s been refined across dozens of GPTs and tens of thousands of prompt iterations — so our mistakes don’t have to be yours.
What GPT‑AJ03 actually does
Enterprise Sleuth is a lens on your data: one part detective, one part analyst, one part explainer. It’s designed for noisy, real‑world enterprises — not tidy demo datasets.
Thinks like an investigator, not a search box

Classic search answers “where is this file?”. Enterprise Sleuth is built to answer “what’s the story here?” and “what changed over time?”. It pulls fragments from policies, project docs, tickets, chats, and meeting notes, then stitches them into timelines and narratives people can actually act on.

It leans on AskJamie’s three personas — detective, analyst, teacher — to keep answers both useful and human. The detective hunts through the haystack. The analyst connects patterns and trade‑offs. The teacher explains it back in clear language so your team doesn’t have to be “AI people” to benefit.

Under the hood, it’s also a prompt architecture: careful guardrails, reasoning steps, and sanity checks that keep the model from drifting off into hallucinations or unhelpful tangents as it works through complex questions.
Six core capabilities it brings to work
Contextual Intelligence Retrieval (CIR) — pulls the right evidence at the right time.
Organizational Cartography Engine (OCE) — maps people, teams, and systems over time.
Implicit Knowledge Mining (IKM) — surfaces the “unwritten rules” hiding in chatter and docs.
Compliance & Governance Correlation (CGC) — lines up decisions with policy and risk context.
Adaptive Discovery Orchestration (ADO) — mutates search strategies when the straight line fails.
Cognitive Companion Interface (CCI) — keeps the voice steady: professional, analytical, slightly wry.
Bring your own platform. The recipes travel.

Underneath the logos, all modern “agent” platforms do a similar thing: they let you save detailed instructions and attach files so the AI behaves like a reusable, specialized tool. Enterprise Sleuth is designed to map cleanly onto all of them.
Plain‑English tour of the ecosystem
If you’re not living in AI blogs every day, the vocabulary gets overwhelming fast. Here’s the simple view:
OpenAI Custom GPTs — your own versions of ChatGPT with saved instructions and up to dozens of attached files. They live inside ChatGPT and can be shared like mini‑apps.

Microsoft Copilot Studio Agents — agents you design inside Microsoft 365 so they can work in Teams, SharePoint, and Office. You describe what they should do and what data they can see, and Copilot carries it out.
Copilot Studio Lite Agents — a lighter, template‑driven way to spin up simpler agents quickly, often surfaced directly inside Microsoft 365 as “apps in chat.”
Google Gemini Gems — “custom experts” you define for Gemini. You give them a name, instructions, and a handful of reference files so they remember how you like things done.

Claude Projects & Artifacts — focused workspaces where Claude can use your uploaded docs plus persistent instructions, and then produce reusable outputs (artifacts) like docs, dashboards, or small tools.
Perplexity Spaces / Labs — project hubs where you combine deep research, your own uploads, and saved instructions so you can revisit and extend work over time.

Different labels, same basic pattern: a saved “personality and job description” plus a pile of relevant evidence. Enterprise Sleuth gives you the playbook for that pattern so you can stand up the same sleuth across whichever platforms your organization already pays for.
More controllable — never fully predictable

A key reality check: no custom GPT, Copilot agent, Gem, or Claude project is ever 100% predictable. They’re more like talented new hires: you can give them a great job description, a good starter pack of examples, and clear boundaries — and then you manage the relationship.

The Enterprise Sleuth approach narrows the behavior band dramatically with structured instructions, examples, and guardrails, but it never pretends the model is a vending machine. You stay in the loop. We simply make that loop faster, safer, and more consistently useful.
How the Sleuth recipes plug in
Start with the same instruction skeleton (identity, mission, rules, workflow, output formats).
Drop it into your platform of choice (Custom GPT, Copilot Studio, Gems, Claude, Perplexity).
Attach your own knowledge: policies, playbooks, project archives, catalogs, or data exports.
Iterate once with your team, then reuse endlessly as a branded, in‑house “AI colleague”.

· Lens System
One voice. Four lenses.
AskJamie™ isn’t an ecosystem of tools. It’s a disciplined way of seeing — an Interpretive Lens System (a structured way to examine a story or challenge from four focused perspectives).
Each lens is a self-contained vantage point on your story or challenge. No data handoffs. No tangled workflows. Just one consistent voice, refracted through four distinct perspectives.
What is an Interpretive Lens System?
AskJamie™ is not a platform or a toolkit. It’s a structured set of perspectives — each one a disciplined method of observing, analyzing, and representing a person, brand, or problem.
Each lens answers a single question: “How should this situation be understood and expressed through the AskJamie voice?”

AskJamie doesn’t merge data across lenses. It doesn’t stitch workflows together or pass state from one domain to another. Instead, it provides four distinct vantage points — four curated mirrors that refract your story or challenge through different angles of clarity.
The system is unified by interpretive logic and voice, not by technical dependency.
Why lenses, not ecosystems?
Glee‑fully Personalizable Tools™ is an ecosystem — interdependent, compounding, and designed for internal handoffs. AskJamie™ deliberately isn’t.
The word “ecosystem” implies:
interdependency and feedback loops
shared substrates and cross‑tool memory
internal commerce or flow between components
emergent behavior when pieces operate together
That’s exactly what Glee‑fully is built for. Those Tools trade context and strengthen one another over time.

AskJamie’s modules are self‑contained. A résumé does not inform a portfolio. A portfolio does not inform enterprise reasoning. BrandGuard™ (our AI brand-voice protection tool) does not secretly rewrite résumé tone.
What they share is the method of interpretation — the way Jamie listens, frames, and speaks on your behalf.
That’s why AskJamie is best understood as a unified interpretive model expressed through multiple domains, rather than as a cluster of connected tools.

Why this lens model works for AskJamie
A. Flexibility without entanglement
Each lens stands on its own. You can use one or all four without worrying about cross‑integration or hidden dependencies.
B. A single voice, infinitely refracted
Like light through a prism, AskJamie’s voice shifts depending on the lens applied — but the core frequency remains consistent: clarity, respect, and calm.
C. Built to scale
New lenses can be added without re‑architecting the system. The model can grow vertically (deeper in a domain) or horizontally (into new sectors) without breaking what already works.
D. Clear expectations
A résumé lens should speak differently than an enterprise lens. A portfolio lens should feel distinct from a brand‑fidelity lens. The lens model keeps those boundaries sharp, on purpose.
Why “lens-system” deserves its own home
The Interpretive Lens System isn’t marketing copy. It’s the conceptual spine of AskJamie.bot.
Creating a dedicated /lens-system/ directory gives visitors a place to understand:
what AskJamie actually is
how each lens expresses a different interpretive mode
how voice consistency is maintained across contexts
how AskJamie differs from the Glee‑fully ecosystem and the OverKill Hill P³ backbone
Over time, this folder becomes the intellectual home for diagrams, tone notes, visual mappings, and future lenses — the architecture behind the voice.
The essence of AskJamie’s approach
You reach for AskJamie when you need to articulate something clearly, represent something faithfully, examine something honestly, or explain something persuasively.
That’s the purpose of the Interpretive Lens System: multiple domains, one voice, zero confusion.
In this architecture, AskJamie becomes what it was always meant to be: the articulate, thoughtful, consistent voice that helps the world understand you — through whichever lens best fits the moment.

What GPT‑BFS01 actually is

A conversational explainer, not a data tap

GPT‑BFS01 does not connect to SAP, Salesforce, email, or internal files. It works entirely from publicly available BFS information — investor reports, BLDR.com, CSR documents, public reviews, relevant codes, and reputable industry sources.
Its job is to teach and clarify: who Builders FirstSource is, what it sells, how it fits into U.S. wood‑frame construction, and how to route users back to official channels.
A BrandGuard™ lens for BFS
This prototype treats “Builders FirstSource” as a protected semantic territory. It keeps answers:
Positive but honest — acknowledging strengths and critiques.
Grounded in public facts — no speculation, no leaks.
Routed to BLDR.com and local branches whenever real‑world action is needed.
In other words: it doesn’t just mention BFS; it defends how BFS is represented when models talk about lumber, windows, doors, trusses, and the broader value stream.
A repeatable chassis, built in ~8 hours
Under the hood, GPT‑BFS01 is a disciplined prompt + corpus architecture:
A carefully written instruction spine that defines identity, guardrails, and tone.
A curated, versioned knowledge pack in markdown — 18 topic files covering BFS products, logistics, codes, sustainability, and more.
A test harness of real‑world prompts that probe both normal and edge‑case behavior.
The same scaffold can be reused to build a Safety Coach, Sustainability Advisor, or Supplier Assistant in a single working day — just by swapping the corpus.
